docs.title: AKAER Autonomous Landing
docs.text:
Projeto de conclusão de curso do Insper em parceria com a Akaer. Treinamos cinco redes neurais feed-forward (uma por comando) para pousar uma Cessna 172P no FlightGear por aprendizado por imitação, com um PID em cascata como linha de base não-IA.

Esta documentação atende a dois públicos:

  • quem precisa reproduzir o experimento atual do zero,
  • futuros alunos que vão estender o projeto com novos modelos (RNN, variantes com 1/2/4/8 redes, comparações).

docs.title: Avisos
docs.text:
Apenas simulação

Todo o código deste projeto é destinado exclusivamente à simulação em FlightGear. Não é um sistema de voo real.

Launcher macOS

scripts/launch_flightgear.sh localiza o aplicativo FlightGear no macOS. Para Linux/Windows, veja Launcher do FlightGear.

docs.title: Contribuindo
docs.text:
Esta seção descreve como o grupo organiza o trabalho no repositório e como estender a documentação.

  • Fluxo de trabalho no repositório — issues, branches e PRs.
  • Fluxo da documentação — como editar e publicar estas páginas.

docs.title: Fluxo no repositório
docs.text:
As próximas etapas vivem nas issues do GitHub: PID, variantes com 1, 2, 4 e 8 redes, RNN, modelo alternativo e comparação dos resultados.

  1. Escolha uma issue e se atribua.
  2. Crie uma branch a partir de main, com nome ligado à issue (ex.: issue-7-rnn).
  3. Trabalhe em commits pequenos e mantenha o CI verde.
  4. Abra um pull request vinculado à issue (Closes #N no corpo).
  5. Peça revisão de pelo menos um colega antes do merge.

Referências do README do projeto a Pfe ak/ correspondem agora a src/, lançadores a scripts/ e saídas a artifacts/.

docs.title: Issues de modelos futuros
docs.text:
Cada modelo planejado tem uma página vazia em explanation/models/future-*.md (ex.: future-rnn.md). Quando a issue for mergeada:

  1. Preencha a página correspondente (PT e EN) usando pid-baseline.md e five-networks.md como gabarito.
  2. Atualize a tabela de modelos em explanation/models/index.md (status → Pronto, link do PR).
  3. Se o modelo mudar o pipeline online, atualize explanation/online-pipeline.md.

docs.title: Fluxo da documentação
docs.text: Como editar, visualizar e publicar as páginas deste site.

docs.title: Instalar as dependências de docs
docs.text:
Dentro do ambiente virtual do projeto:

python -m pip install -r docs/requirements.txt

As versões ficam presas em docs/requirements.txt para que o build local e o CI batam.

docs.title: Editar e visualizar
docs.text:
mkdocs serve

Abre http://127.0.0.1:8000. O servidor recarrega sozinho a cada edição. Troque entre PT e EN no seletor do topo (ícone de idioma).

docs.title: Build de verificação
docs.text:
Antes de abrir o PR:

mkdocs build --strict

Deve passar com zero warnings. O CI roda a mesma linha em .github/workflows/docs.yml.

docs.title: Regra bilíngue
docs.text:
• PT é a língua padrão: arquivo pagina.md.
  • EN usa o sufixo: arquivo pagina.en.md.
  • Toda página existe nas duas línguas. A estrutura (seções, tabelas, diagramas) é idêntica — só o texto muda.
  • nav em mkdocs.yml lista só os arquivos PT; o plugin mkdocs-static-i18n descobre o par .en.md automaticamente.

docs.title: Convenções de escrita
docs.text:
• Cada página começa com uma linha de resumo e uma lista do que o leitor vai conseguir fazer.
  • Blocos de código no lugar de screenshots para qualquer coisa digitável; screenshots só para UI do FlightGear.
  • Admonitions: !!! note para contexto, !!! warning para o launcher macOS-only e CSVs de voos danificados, !!! tip para atalhos.
  • Todo how-to termina com um bloco Saída esperada que o leitor pode comparar.
  • Diagramas em mermaid inline (não imagens); screenshots viram arquivos em docs/assets/screenshots/.

docs.title: Deploy
docs.text:
A publicação é feita em duas etapas porque o repositório de código é privado e o plano gratuito do Vercel não serve repositórios privados de organização.

  1. Build no GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/docs.yml): a cada push em main que toque docs/**, mkdocs.yml, src/** ou o próprio workflow, o Action instala as dependências e roda mkdocs build --strict.
  2. Push para um espelho público: o Action publica o site/ gerado no repositório público hhenriqueN/akaer-landing-docs (branch main, histórico órfão — cada deploy sobrescreve o anterior).
  3. Vercel serve o espelho: o projeto Vercel está conectado em hhenriqueN/akaer-landing-docs, sem build command — ele só entrega os HTMLs estáticos a partir da raiz do repo.

Para que o Action consiga empurrar no espelho, o repo privado guarda o segredo DOCS_DEPLOY_PAT (um fine-grained Personal Access Token com Contents: Read & write restrito ao espelho). Se o token expirar, gere outro em https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens e substitua o segredo.

docs.title: Modelo novo
docs.text:
Quando a issue de um modelo futuro for mergeada:

  1. Preencha explanation/models/future-<nome>.md e .en.md (hoje são placeholders com só o título).
  2. Atualize a tabela em explanation/models/index.md.
  3. Se o modelo altera o pipeline online, atualize explanation/online-pipeline.md.
  4. Se adiciona um novo script, inclua em reference/cli.md.

docs.title: Explicação
docs.text:
Material para entender como e por que o sistema funciona:

  • Arquitetura — visão geral do fluxo de dados.
  • Aprendizado por imitação — por que behavioral cloning, split de dados, limites.
  • Pipeline online — filtro, resample, z-score, máquina de fases.
  • Pipeline offline — do .fgtape aos folds normalizados.
  • Modelos — o que já existe (ANN, PID) e o que está planejado.

docs.title: Arquitetura
docs.text: Dois caminhos: offline (treino) e online (voo).

docs.title: Caminho online (em voo)
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  FG[FlightGear 60 Hz] -- "UDP 5501" --> IF[fg_interface.receive_all]
  IF --> LP["Butterworth 2ª ordem · 4 Hz"]
  LP --> ZOH[Zero-order hold · 10 Hz]
  ZOH --> FT["Features (lat__, lon__)"]
  FT --> N["z-score (clip ±5)"]
  N --> M{Controlador}
  M --> |"5 redes"| NN["aileron · rudder · elevator · throttle · flaps"]
  M --> |"PID"| PID["malhas em cascata"]
  NN --> POS[Pós-processo: clip, elevator-trim, regra do freio]
  PID --> POS
  POS -- "UDP 5502 · 10 Hz" --> FG

Detalhes em Pipeline online.

docs.title: Caminho offline (treino)
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  TAPE["Data/raw/*.fgtape"] -->|scripts/fgtape_to_csv.py| CSV["Data/csv/voos-piloto/*.csv (60 Hz)"]
  CSV -->|baseline-model externo| FOLDS["Data/processed/normalized_folds/fold_00_*.csv (10 Hz z-scored)"]
  FOLDS -->|src/ann.py| MODELS["artifacts/*.pt + normalization.json"]
  MODELS -->|src/replay.py| REPLAY["replay_*.png (malha aberta)"]
  MODELS -->|src/fly.py| FG["FlightGear (malha fechada)"]

Detalhes em Pipeline offline.

docs.title: Pontos-chave
docs.text: Decisão Onde Por quê 60 → 10 Hz com filtro de 4 Hz fly.py + folds Alinha online e offline; remove ruído > 30 Hz do simulador Normalização única em JSON artifacts/normalization.json Treino e inferência leem o mesmo arquivo — difícil divergir 5 redes independentes src/ann.py Simples, interpretável, serve de linha de base para variantes futuras Lags de 0,5 / 1,0 / 1,5 s HISTORY_LAGS em ann.py e buffer live em fly.py Dá temporalidade a um feed-forward sem usar RNN Elevator = yoke + trim fly.py + rede elevator A rede aprende o movimento efetivo; fly.py desconta o trim antes de mandar ao sim Freio por regra fly.py fase landing Nenhum voo gravado tem "freio" bem comportado para aprender

docs.title: Aprendizado por imitação
docs.text: O projeto usa behavioral cloning (BC): aprender a função que mapeia estado → comando a partir de demonstrações do piloto.

docs.title: Dados
docs.text:
Conjunto Voos Uso Treino 11 voos de fold_00_train.csv Atualiza os pesos Validação voo-normal2, voo-com-8-nos Escolhe a melhor época (sem gradiente) Teste voo-2-com-16-nos Nunca entra em ann.py; usado em replay.py

O split é por voo inteiro, não por frames. Isso evita vazamento de contexto temporal entre splits.

docs.title: Alvo e perda
docs.text:
Cada rede prevê um comando contínuo:

Rede Coluna-alvo Comando físico aileron laty__aileron_command aileron (-1..1) rudder laty__rudder_command leme (-1..1) elevator lony__elevator_effective manche + trim (-1..1) throttle lony__throttle_command manete (0..1) flaps lon__flaps_state_norm posição de flaps (0..1)

Perda MSE sobre o alvo z-scored, otimizador Adam (lr=1e-3), MAX_EPOCHS=1000, BATCH_SIZE=1000, seed fixo (0).

Baseline comparativo impresso em ann.py: RMSE de "chutar sempre a média do piloto". Toda rede que vale a pena deve ficar significativamente abaixo dessa linha.

docs.title: Por que BC e não RL
docs.text:
• Temos dezenas de demonstrações de pouso, não um reward denso.
  • Treino é determinístico e barato (CPU basta).
  • Linha de base clara para comparar com variantes futuras (RNN, Dagger, RL).

docs.title: Limites conhecidos
docs.text:
• Compounding error / covariate shift: em malha fechada, pequenos desvios levam a estados que a rede nunca viu no treino. Replay (malha aberta) não detecta isso. Só o teste no FlightGear detecta.
  • Freio: nenhuma rede aprende frear bem — o piloto freia tarde e abrupto. fly.py usa regra: brake=0.7 quando GS < 45 kt na fase landing.
  • Fase landing: assim que todas as rodas estão no chão por 0,5 s, as redes não comandam mais aileron/rudder/throttle; fly.py força zero. Isso evita que a rede acelere ou cambalhote no solo.
  • Vento forte com dano: dois voos de treino (voo-2-com-16-nos, voo-3-com-16-nos) têm flags de dano. Útil para teste; perigoso como demonstração "limpa".

Ver Pipeline online para a parte do loop que lida com esses limites na prática.

docs.title: Pipeline offline
docs.text:
Como as gravações do piloto viram dados prontos para treino.

flowchart LR
  FG[Simulador grava .fgtape] --> TAPE["Data/raw/*.fgtape"]
  TAPE -->|scripts/fgtape_to_csv.py| CSV["Data/csv/voos-piloto/*.csv (60 Hz · Δt variável)"]
  CSV -->|repo externo baseline-model| FOLDS["Data/processed/normalized_folds/fold_00_{train,val}.csv (10 Hz · z-scored)"]
  FOLDS -->|src/ann.py| MODELS["artifacts/*.pt + normalization.json"]

docs.title: Estágio 1 — .fgtape → CSV cru
docs.text:
scripts/fgtape_to_csv.py:

  • parser puro em Python (stdlib),
  • lê o cabeçalho XML com ~245 propriedades,
  • descomprime frames DEFLATE,
  • escreve CSV com frame, sim_time e 245 colunas.

Esquema completo: Colunas do fgtape, Colunas dos voos do piloto.

Δt variável

sim_time depende do FPS do simulador no momento da gravação (geralmente 40–60 Hz). Não trate as linhas como passos de tempo constantes.

docs.title: Estágio 2 — CSV → folds normalizados
docs.text:
Processamento feito em repositório externo:

  • github.com/hhenriqueN/baseline-model

Esse pipeline:

  • reamostra 60 Hz → 10 Hz (grade fixa),
  • deriva features em frame da pista (along-track, cross-track, erros de rampa, flare flag),
  • z-score por feature com clip a ±5,
  • gera fold_{NN}_{train,val}.csv em Data/processed/normalized_folds/,
  • grava artifacts/normalization.json com os parâmetros usados.

Mesmas features e mesmo JSON de normalização são usados em src/fly.py — ponto crítico para evitar divergência entre treino e inferência.

Treino atual usa só fold_00

src/ann.py lê fold_00_train.csv + fold_00_val.csv, que juntos cobrem os 13 voos. Folds 01-04 existem no repo externo mas não são usados hoje.

docs.title: Estágio 3 — folds → modelos
docs.text:
python src/ann.py (ver Cinco redes neurais).

Produz artifacts/<rede>.pt com pesos + metadados que src/fly.py consome em produção. A normalização de alvos é calculada durante o treino e salva no .pt; a normalização de entradas vem do normalization.json externo.

docs.title: Voos usados
docs.text:
13 sessões em Data/csv/voos-piloto/ (circuitos completos, aproximações normais, voos com vento 0 / 8 / 16 kt).

  • Treino: 11 voos.
  • Validação: voo-normal2, voo-com-8-nos.
  • Teste: voo-2-com-16-nos (nunca entra em ann.py).

Voos com dano

voo-2-com-16-nos.csv e voo-3-com-16-nos.csv apresentam flags de dano em asa/trem. Vale conferir antes de usar como demonstração "limpa". Ver Colunas dos voos do piloto.

docs.title: Pipeline online
docs.text: Como src/fly.py processa dados em tempo real.

docs.title: Taxas
docs.text: Estágio Taxa FlightGear envia pacotes 60 Hz fly.py lê e filtra 60 Hz (nenhum pacote descartado) fly.py reamostra para a grade de inferência 10 Hz fly.py envia comandos 10 Hz

docs.title: Etapas detalhadas
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  P["Pacote UDP 60 Hz"] --> B["Butterworth 2ª ordem · 4 Hz"]
  B --> Z["ZOH · amostra a cada 0,1 s"]
  Z --> F["Features em frame da pista (along-track, cross-track, erro de rampa, flare flag, ...)"]
  F --> N["z-score + clip ±5 (artifacts/normalization.json)"]
  N --> H["Buffer com lags 5/10/15 ticks"]
  H --> R["5 redes"]
  R --> C["Pós-processo"]
  C --> U["UDP 5502"]

docs.title: 1. Filtro passa-baixas
docs.text: Butterworth de 2ª ordem, cutoff 4 Hz, causal (fly.py:81-102). Elimina ruído de alta frequência do simulador (jitter de física/renderização).

docs.title: 2. Zero-order hold a 10 Hz
docs.text: A cada 0,1 s, fly.py toma o último valor filtrado disponível. Grade fixa, idêntica ao frame_10hz dos folds de treino.

docs.title: 3. Features da pista
docs.text: fly.py converte lat/lon em coordenadas da pista 02 (along-track, cross-track em metros) e calcula erros de rampa, altura sobre o threshold, etc. Nomes das colunas são idênticos aos do treino (lat__*, lon__*).

docs.title: 4. z-score com clip
docs.text: Lê artifacts/normalization.json: (x - mean) / std, clip a ±5. Features com entrada null no JSON (sin/cos, flaps_state_norm, flare_flag) não são z-scored.

docs.title: 5. Lags temporais
docs.text: Buffer live com 5, 10, 15 ticks (0,5, 1,0, 1,5 s). Antes de ter histórico suficiente, repete o primeiro valor — mesma convenção do add_history em ann.py.

docs.title: 6. Inferência
docs.text:
As cinco redes rodam a cada 0,1 s. Entradas:

Rede Entradas aileron, rudder 11 features lat__* × 4 (atual + 3 lags) = 44 elevator, throttle 12 features lon__* × 4 = 48 flaps 4 features × 4 = 16

docs.title: 7. Pós-processo
docs.text:
• Todas saídas: clip em [-1, 1] (ou [0, 1] para throttle, flaps, brake).
  • elevator: a rede saiu elevator_effective (yoke + trim). fly.py subtrai o elevator_trim recebido do FlightGear antes de enviar.
  • throttle: enviado também em throttle0 (para cobrir variações de aeronave).

docs.title: Máquina de fases
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> final_approach
  final_approach --> flare: AGL ≤ 20 ft
  flare --> landing: wheels on ground ≥ 0,5 s
  landing --> [*]
Fase Redes ativas Regras final_approach todas — flare todas — landing nenhuma de aileron/rudder/throttle brake = 0.7 se GS < 45 kt; aileron, rudder, throttle forçados a 0

Transições são monotônicas (uma vez em flare, não volta para final_approach).

docs.title: Encerramento
docs.text: fly.py continua logando até detectar touchdown estável; depois escreve artifacts/flights/<nome>_<timestamp>.csv e encerra. O FlightGear precisa ser fechado manualmente.

docs.title: Modelos
docs.text:
Esta é a matriz de modelos do projeto. Cada linha aponta para a página correspondente.

Modelo Status Issue / PR Arquivos Notas Cinco redes neurais (uma por comando) Pronto merged src/ann.py, src/fly.py Linha de base atual PID (baseline não-IA) Pronto #10 src/pid.py, src/fly_pid.py Referência de comparação RNN Planejado issues — — 1 rede única Planejado issues — — 2 redes (lat/lon) Planejado issues — — 4 redes Planejado issues — — 8 redes Planejado issues — —

Para implementar uma variante, siga Adicionar um novo modelo.

docs.title: Cinco redes neurais
docs.text: Linha de base atual do projeto. Uma rede feed-forward por comando.

docs.title: Arquitetura
docs.text:
Todas as cinco redes têm a mesma estrutura:

Linear(n_inputs, 64) → ReLU → Linear(64, 64) → ReLU → Linear(64, 1)
  • Perda: MSE sobre o alvo z-scored.
  • Otimizador: Adam, lr = 1e-3.
  • MAX_EPOCHS = 1000, BATCH_SIZE = 1000, seed fixo (0).
  • Melhor época selecionada pelo erro de validação (early stopping passivo).

docs.title: Entradas por rede
docs.text:
Rede Grupo Nº features base Com lags (×4) aileron lat__* 11 44 rudder lat__* 11 44 elevator lon__* 12 48 throttle lon__* 12 48 flaps 4 fixas 4 16

Lags: 0,5 / 1,0 / 1,5 s = 5 / 10 / 15 ticks (HISTORY_LAGS). Cada feature entra como "agora" + "lag@5" + "lag@10" + "lag@15".

Features base: ver Folds normalizados.

docs.title: Saídas
docs.text:
Rede Coluna-alvo Alvo físico aileron laty__aileron_command aileron (-1..1) rudder laty__rudder_command leme (-1..1) elevator lony__elevator_effective manche + trim; fly.py subtrai o trim antes de enviar throttle lony__throttle_command manete (0..1) flaps lon__flaps_state_norm posição de flaps (0..1)

Alvo é z-scored durante o treino com média e desvio do conjunto de treino; esses valores são salvos em artifacts/<rede>.pt como y_mean, y_std e usados em fly.py para desfazer a normalização.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
Cada artifacts/<rede>.pt guarda:

Chave Conteúdo model state_dict do PyTorch input_cols Lista completa de colunas de entrada (com sufixos @5, @10, @15) output_cols Nome da coluna-alvo y_mean, y_std Normalização do alvo (treino) best_epoch Época escolhida validation_flights Voos usados para selecionar a melhor época

fly.py lê o checkpoint com torch.load(..., weights_only=False).

docs.title: Por que cinco redes
docs.text:
• Transparência: cada rede é pequena, treina rápido (CPU basta) e é fácil inspecionar.
  • Diagnóstico: curvas de aprendizado separadas revelam qual comando é mais difícil (flaps costuma ser o mais fácil; elevator, o mais sensível).
  • Linha de base: variantes futuras (1, 2, 4, 8 redes, RNN) são comparadas contra esta.

docs.title: Quando revisar
docs.text:
• Taxa de amostragem (10 Hz) ou lags (5/10/15) mudarem — reconstruir o pipeline em fly.py e refazer os folds no repo externo.
  • normalization.json mudar — refazer o treino inteiro.
  • Adicionar/remover features — alterar NETWORKS em ann.py e as features em fly.py, nos mesmos nomes.

docs.title: PID (baseline)
docs.text: Controlador em cascata, sem redes neurais, para servir de linha de comparação.

docs.title: Objetivo
docs.text: Mostrar que o cenário é controlável com controle clássico bem ajustado — e dar uma referência honesta de desempenho que modelos de IA precisam, no mínimo, igualar.

docs.title: Estrutura em cascata
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  CT[Desvio lateral da pista] --> HD[Erro de proa]
  HD --> BK[Inclinação alvo]
  BK --> AI[Aileron]

  SS[Derrapagem] --> RD[Rudder]

  H[Altura em relação à rampa 3°] --> VS[Razão de descida alvo]
  VS --> PI[Arfagem alvo]
  PI --> EL[Elevator]

  V[Velocidade indicada] --> TH[Throttle]
  • Lateral (aproximação): desvio lateral → erro de proa → inclinação → aileron. Derrapagem → rudder.
  • Longitudinal: altura em relação à rampa de 3° (ponto de visada 300 m após a cabeceira) → razão de descida → arfagem → elevator.
  • Velocidade: airspeed → throttle (Vref 65 kt).
  • Flaps: fixos em 1.0 (mesma configuração dos voos gravados).

No flare (AGL ≤ 20 ft):

  • razão de descida alvo passa a decair exponencialmente (vs_ref = -agl / 3.0 com piso de 1,5 fpm),
  • throttle vai a idle,
  • rudder tenta alinhar a proa,
  • aileron zera a deriva lateral.

docs.title: PID em forma de velocidade
docs.text:
src/pid.py implementa o mesmo PID discreto do autopilot do FlightGear ($FG_ROOT/Docs/README.digitalfilters):

ep_n       = beta * r_n - y_n           (proporcional)
e_n        = r_n - y_n                  (integral)
ed_n       = gamma * r_n - y_n          (derivativo, filtrado)
Δu_n       = Kp * [ (ep_n - ep_{n-1})
                   + Ts/Ti * e_n
                   + Td/Ts * (edf_n - 2*edf_{n-1} + edf_{n-2}) ]
u_n        = clamp(u_{n-1} + Δu_n, u_min, u_max)

Parâmetros por malha: Kp, Ti, Td, u_min, u_max, beta (peso do setpoint na proporção), alpha (filtro derivativo Tf = alpha * Td), gamma (peso do setpoint na derivada; 0 = derivada só sobre a medida).

A forma de velocidade elimina o estado integral — o anti-windup fica no clamp da saída.

docs.title: Diferenças práticas em relação às redes
docs.text: Item Redes (fly.py) PID (fly_pid.py) Entrada pacotes UDP filtrados a 4 Hz pacotes UDP brutos Reamostragem ZOH para 10 Hz último pacote a cada 0,1 s Normalização z-score com normalization.json nenhuma Taxa de comando 10 Hz 10 Hz Fases final_approach → flare → landing iguais Freio regra (brake=0.7 se GS < 45 kt) mesma regra

docs.title: Por que não usar o PID interno do FlightGear
docs.text: O autopilot do FlightGear escreve direto em /controls/*, bypass do UDP e sem a taxa de 10 Hz usada pelas redes — a comparação ficaria injusta. fly_pid.py recria o PID em Python mantendo o mesmo loop e os mesmos limites.

docs.title: Ganhos
docs.text:
Os onze PIDs têm ganhos tunados para a dinâmica do C172P na pista 02 de BIKF. Vivem em GAINS dentro de src/fly_pid.py e são salvos ao lado de cada log em artifacts/flights/pid_<timestamp>.json.

Mudar ganhos: edite GAINS, rode CONTROLLER=pid bash scripts/run_flight.sh ..., compare pelo log.

docs.title: Começando
docs.text:
Tutorial em dois passos para quem nunca rodou o projeto:

  1. Instalação — Python, dependências e FlightGear.
  2. Primeiro pouso — do git clone ao pouso no simulador.

Depois disso, use as receitas em Como fazer.

docs.title: Primeiro pouso
docs.text:
Objetivo: do zero a um pouso autônomo no FlightGear. Pré-requisito: Instalação concluída.

Resultado esperado:

  • cinco arquivos .pt em artifacts/,

docs.title: ann
docs.text:
One ANN per control, trained on the report's data (Data/processed/normalized_folds/).

python src/ann.py

aileron, rudder     <- the 11 lateral inputs      (lat__...)
elevator, throttle  <- the 12 longitudinal inputs (lon__...)
flaps               <- where the aircraft is and how fast

Every network has the same structure (inputs -> 64 -> 64 -> 1 output) and the same loss (MSE).

Short memory: every network sees its inputs now AND 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 s ago (HISTORY_LAGS), so it can see how the aircraft is moving, not only where it is. fly.py keeps the same buffer live.

Data split, by whole flights: train 11 flights validation 2 flights (VALIDATION_FLIGHTS): all MAX_EPOCHS epochs are trained, and the weights of the epoch with the lowest validation loss are the ones kept test voo-2-com-16-nos, never used here: python src/replay.py voo-2-com-16-nos

Writes artifacts/.pt (loaded by fly.py) and artifacts/_learning_curve.png.

The inputs in Data/processed/normalized_folds/ are ALREADY z-scored, so they are used as they are. The targets are raw, so they are normalized here.

def input_columns(data, spec):
    """A prefix ("lat__") means every column that starts with it; a list is used as it is."""
    if isinstance(spec, str):
        return [c for c in data.columns if c.startswith(spec)]
    return spec

docs.title: add_history
docs.text:
add_history(data, base_cols)

Adds the inputs as they were HISTORY_LAGS ticks ago, e.g. "lat__roll_deg@5" = 0.5 s ago.

Built per flight and by frame number (not by row). A missing frame takes the last value before it; before the first row of a flight, the first value is repeated, which is what fly.py does when it takes control and has no past yet. Returns the data with the new columns, and the full list of input columns.

Source code in src/ann.py 
def add_history(data, base_cols):
    """Adds the inputs as they were HISTORY_LAGS ticks ago, e.g. "lat__roll_deg@5" = 0.5 s ago.

    Built per flight and by frame number (not by row). A missing frame takes the last value
    before it; before the first row of a flight, the first value is repeated, which is what
    fly.py does when it takes control and has no past yet.
    Returns the data with the new columns, and the full list of input columns."""
    flights = []
    for _, g in data.groupby("episode_id", sort=False):
        g = g.sort_values("frame_10hz").copy()
        frames = g["frame_10hz"].to_numpy()
        every_frame = g.set_index("frame_10hz")[base_cols].reindex(range(frames[0], frames[-1] + 1)).ffill()
        for lag in HISTORY_LAGS:
            past = every_frame.shift(lag).bfill()
            g[[f"{c}@{lag}" for c in base_cols]] = past.loc[frames].to_numpy()
        flights.append(g)
    input_cols = base_cols + [f"{c}@{lag}" for lag in HISTORY_LAGS for c in base_cols]
    return pd.concat(flights), input_cols

docs.title: fg_interface
docs.text:
Moves flight data and control commands between FlightGear and the autopilot over UDP, using FlightGear's generic protocol (fg/pfe_out.xml, fg/pfe_in.xml).

FlightGear --(flight data, UDP 5501, 60 Hz)--> autopilot --(commands, UDP 5502, 10 Hz)--> FlightGear

FlightGear sends at 60 Hz, the rate of the pilot recordings, because the report's pipeline low-pass filters the 60 Hz data before taking one sample every 0.1 s (see fly.py).

docs.title: FlightGearLink
docs.text:
Source code in src/fg_interface.py 
class FlightGearLink:
    def __init__(self, host: str = HOST, data_port: int = DATA_PORT, command_port: int = COMMAND_PORT):
        self.rx = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
        self.rx.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
        self.rx.bind((host, data_port))
        self.tx = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
        self.target = (host, command_port)

    def receive_all(self, timeout: float | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        """Every flight-data packet waiting, oldest first. [] on timeout.

        Nothing is skipped: the low-pass filter in fly.py needs every 60 Hz sample.
        """

    def _parse(data: bytes) -> dict | None:
        line = data.decode("ascii", "ignore").strip().splitlines()[-1]
        values = line.split(",")
        if len(values) != len(OUT_FIELDS):
            return None

        o = {k: float(v) for k, v in zip(OUT_FIELDS, values)}
        o["wow"] = int(max(o["wow_nose"], o["wow_left"], o["wow_right"]) > 0)     # any wheel on the ground
        o["wow_main"] = int(max(o["wow_left"], o["wow_right"]) > 0)              # main gear only
        o["t"] = o["sim_time"]
        return o

    def send(self, c: dict):
        """Send one set of commands.

        `elevator` is the YOKE position. The longitudinal network outputs
        elevator_effective (yoke + trim), so the controller must send
        elevator = elevator_effective - elevator_trim.
        """

        v = dict(aileron=c["aileron"], elevator=c["elevator"], rudder=c["rudder"], throttle=c["throttle"],
                 throttle0=c["throttle"], flaps=c["flaps"], brake_left=c["brake"], brake_right=c["brake"])
        self.tx.sendto((",".join(f"{v[k]:.5f}" for k in IN_FIELDS) + "\n").encode("ascii"), self.target)

    def close(self):
        self.rx.close()
        self.tx.close()

class LowPass:
    """2nd-order Butterworth low-pass, causal:
        y[n] = b0 x[n] + b1 x[n-1] + b2 x[n-2] - a1 y[n-1] - a2 y[n-2]
    Coefficients from the bilinear transform (the same as scipy.signal.butter(2, fc, fs=fs))."""

    def __init__(self, cutoff_hz=CUTOFF_HZ, sample_hz=SAMPLE_HZ):
        k = math.tan(math.pi * cutoff_hz / sample_hz)
        norm = 1.0 / (1.0 + math.sqrt(2.0) * k + k * k)
        self.b0 = k * k * norm
        self.b1 = 2.0 * self.b0
        self.b2 = self.b0
        self.a1 = 2.0 * (k * k - 1.0) * norm
        self.a2 = (1.0 - math.sqrt(2.0) * k + k * k) * norm
        self.x1 = self.x2 = self.y1 = self.y2 = None

    def __call__(self, x):
        if self.x1 is None:         # start at rest on the first value: no start-up transient
            self.x1 = self.x2 = self.y1 = self.y2 = x
        y = self.b0 * x + self.b1 * self.x1 + self.b2 * self.x2 - self.a1 * self.y1 - self.a2 * self.y2
        self.x2, self.x1 = self.x1, x
        self.y2, self.y1 = self.y1, y
        return y

class ReportFeatures:
    """60 Hz packets in, the report's variables out every 0.1 s.

    Zero-order hold, as in the report: the value at grid time t_k is the last filtered sample
    with t_n <= t_k. So grid point k is known when the first sample AFTER t_k arrives.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.filters = {name: LowPass() for name in FILTERED}
        self.state = None           # filtered values of the latest sample
        self.next_tick = None       # time of the next 10 Hz grid point
        self.heading_prev = None
        self.heading_unwrapped = 0.0
        self.glideslope_error = 0.0

    def add_sample(self, o):
        """Feed one packet. Returns the features of the grid points it closes (usually 0 or 1)."""
        if self.next_tick is None:
            self.next_tick = o["t"]             # the grid starts at the first sample

        ticks = []
        while self.state is not None and o["t"] > self.next_tick + 1e-6:
            ticks.append(self.features(self.next_tick))
            self.next_tick += GRID_S

        # heading is filtered unwrapped, or 359 -> 1 deg would pass through 180 deg
        if self.heading_prev is None:
            self.heading_unwrapped = o["heading"]
        else:
            self.heading_unwrapped += wrap180(o["heading"] - self.heading_prev)
        self.heading_prev = o["heading"]

        raw = dict(o, heading=self.heading_unwrapped)
        self.state = {name: self.filters[name](raw[name]) for name in FILTERED}
        for name in ["flaps", "wow", "elevator_trim", "crashed"]:     # not filtered
            self.state[name] = o[name]
        return ticks

    def features(self, t):
        s = self.state
        along, cross = to_runway_frame(s["lat"], s["lon"])
        heading_error = wrap180(s["heading"] - RUNWAY["heading_deg"])
        height_above_threshold = s["alt_ft"] - RUNWAY["elevation_ft"]

        distance = -along           # to the threshold, during the approach
        if distance >= GLIDESLOPE_HOLD_M:
            self.glideslope_error = math.degrees(math.atan2(0.3048 * height_above_threshold, distance)) \
                - GLIDESLOPE_REF_DEG

        return dict(
            t=t,
            # ---- the report's variables, named as in Data/processed/normalized_folds/ (without lat__ / lon__)
            along_track_m=along,
            cross_track_error_m=cross,
            heading_error_sin=math.sin(math.radians(heading_error)),
            heading_error_cos=math.cos(math.radians(heading_error)),
            agl_ft=s["agl_ft"],
            roll_deg=s["roll"],
            sideslip_rad=s["side_slip_rad"],
            roll_rate_degps=s["roll_rate"],
            yaw_rate_degps=s["yaw_rate"],
            airspeed_kt=s["ias"],
            lateral_body_speed_fps=s["v_lateral_fps"],
            glideslope_error_deg=self.glideslope_error,
            height_above_threshold_ft=height_above_threshold,
            pitch_deg=s["pitch"],
            alpha_deg=s["alpha"],
            pitch_rate_degps=s["pitch_rate"],
            airspeed_error_kt=s["ias"] - V_REF_KT,
            vertical_speed_fps=s["vs_fps"],
            flaps_state_norm=s["flaps"],
            flare_flag=int(s["agl_ft"] <= FLARE_AGL_FT),
            # ---- for the flight manager and the log
            heading_error_deg=heading_error,
            gs_kt=s["gs_kt"],
            wow=s["wow"],
            elevator_trim=s["elevator_trim"],
            crashed=s["crashed"],
        )

class Net:
    """One network saved by ann.py. Its inputs are z-scored with the report's
    normalization (artifacts/normalization.json), exactly as in Data/processed/normalized_folds/."""

    def __init__(self, name, normalization):
        c = torch.load(OUTPUT_DIR / f"{name}.pt", weights_only=False)
        self.inputs = c["input_cols"]           # e.g. "lat__roll_deg" and "lat__roll_deg@5" (0.5 s ago)
        self.outputs = c["output_cols"]         # e.g. "laty__aileron_command"

        # short memory: the inputs now, and as they were `lag` ticks ago
        self.base_inputs = [col for col in self.inputs if "@" not in col]
        self.lags = sorted({int(col.split("@")[1]) for col in self.inputs if "@" in col})
        self.history = deque(maxlen=max(self.lags, default=0) + 1)      # newest last
        self.y_mean, self.y_std = c["y_mean"], c["y_std"]
        self.clip = normalization["clip"]
        self.norm = normalization["columns"]

        # same shape as in ann.py: inputs -> hidden -> hidden -> outputs
        hidden = c["model"]["0.weight"].shape[0]
        self.model = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(len(self.inputs), hidden),
            nn.ReLU(),

            nn.Linear(hidden, hidden),
            nn.ReLU(),

            nn.Linear(hidden, len(self.outputs))
        )
        self.model.load_state_dict(c["model"])
        self.model.eval()

    def normalized_inputs(self, f):
        """The current inputs (no history), z-scored as in Data/processed/normalized_folds/."""
        x = []
        for col in self.base_inputs:
            value = f[col.split("__")[1]]
            n = self.norm[col]
            if n is not None:                   # sin, cos, flaps and flare_flag are not z-scored
                value = min(max((value - n["mean"]) / n["std"], -self.clip), self.clip)
            x.append(value)
        return np.array(x)

    def __call__(self, f):
        """Called once per 10 Hz tick: the current inputs join the history."""
        self.history.append(self.normalized_inputs(f))

        # before there is enough past (just after taking control), the oldest value is repeated,
        # as in training at the start of every flight
        x = [self.history[-1]]
        for lag in self.lags:
            x.append(self.history[max(len(self.history) - 1 - lag, 0)])
        x = np.concatenate(x)

        with torch.no_grad():
            y = self.model(torch.tensor(x, dtype=torch.float32)).numpy()
        y = y * self.y_std + self.y_mean                     # back to real units
        return {col.split("__")[1]: float(v) for col, v in zip(self.outputs, y)}

class Autopilot:

    def __init__(self):
        normalization = json.load(open(OUTPUT_DIR / "normalization.json"))
        self.features = ReportFeatures()
        # one network per control
        self.nets = {name: Net(name, normalization)
                     for name in ["aileron", "rudder", "elevator", "throttle", "flaps"]}

        self.phase = "final_approach"
        self.wow_since = None       # when the wheels last came down
        self.flaps = None           # held where the air phase left it after touchdown
        self.elevator = 0.0         # yoke; held where the flare left it after touchdown

    def on_packet(self, o):
        """Feed one 60 Hz packet. Returns [(features, command)] for every 10 Hz tick it closes."""
        return [(f, self.step(f)) for f in self.features.add_sample(o)]

    def step(self, f):
        if self.flaps is None:
            self.flaps = f["flaps_state_norm"]

        # ---- phase: final approach -> flare -> landing, never back
        if f["wow"] == 1:
            self.wow_since = self.wow_since if self.wow_since is not None else f["t"]
        else:
            self.wow_since = None
        if self.phase != "landing" and self.wow_since is not None \
                and f["t"] - self.wow_since >= TOUCHDOWN_HOLD_S - 1e-6:
            self.phase = "landing"
        elif self.phase == "final_approach" and f["flare_flag"] == 1:
            self.phase = "flare"
        f["phase"] = self.phase

        if self.phase != "landing":
            aileron = self.nets["aileron"](f)["aileron_command"]
            rudder = self.nets["rudder"](f)["rudder_command"]

            # the network gives yoke + trim; the trim wheel stays where it is
            self.elevator = self.nets["elevator"](f)["elevator_effective"] - f["elevator_trim"]
            throttle = self.nets["throttle"](f)["throttle_command"]

            self.flaps = self.nets["flaps"](f)["flaps_state_norm"]

            brake = 0.0
        else:
            # on the ground: no networks were trained for the roll-out, so rules
            aileron = 0.0
            rudder = 0.0
            throttle = 0.0
            brake = BRAKE_LEVEL if f["gs_kt"] < BRAKE_BELOW_KT else 0.0

        return dict(
            aileron=clip(aileron),
            elevator=clip(self.elevator),
            rudder=clip(rudder),
            throttle=clip(throttle, 0.0, 1.0),
            flaps=clip(self.flaps, 0.0, 1.0),
            brake=clip(brake, 0.0, 1.0),
        )

def to_runway_frame(lat, lon):
    """(lat, lon) -> (along track, cross track) in metres from the threshold.
    along: negative before the threshold. cross: positive right of the centreline."""
    p = math.radians(RUNWAY["lat"])
    m_per_deg_lat = 111132.92 - 559.82 * math.cos(2 * p) + 1.175 * math.cos(4 * p)
    m_per_deg_lon = 111412.84 * math.cos(p) - 93.5 * math.cos(3 * p)

    north = (lat - RUNWAY["lat"]) * m_per_deg_lat
    east = (lon - RUNWAY["lon"]) * m_per_deg_lon
    h = math.radians(RUNWAY["heading_deg"])
    return north * math.cos(h) + east * math.sin(h), east * math.cos(h) - north * math.sin(h)

def run(pilot, name="fly", config=None):
    """The loop with FlightGear, for any controller with on_packet(o) -> [(features, command)].
    The log goes to artifacts/flights/<name>_<time>.csv; `config` (e.g. the gains) next to it as .json."""
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)

    link = FlightGearLink()
    print(f"{name} ready - waiting for FlightGear flight data on UDP 5501 (60 Hz) ...")

    log, started, stopped_since, last_print, done = [], False, None, 0.0, False
    try:
        while not done:
            packets = link.receive_all(timeout=5.0)
            if not packets:
                if started:
                    print("no data from FlightGear for 5 s - stopping.")
                    break
                continue

            for o in packets:
                if not started:
                    # FlightGear already streams while it is loading the scenery:
                    # wait for an aircraft that is actually flying
                    if o["ias"] < 30.0 or o["agl_ft"] < 100.0 or o["t"] <= 0.0:
                        continue
                    started = True
                    print(f"taking control at {o['agl_ft']:.0f} ft, {o['ias']:.0f} kt")

                for f, command in pilot.on_packet(o):
                    link.send(command)
                    log.append({**f, **{f"cmd_{k}": v for k, v in command.items()}})

                    if f["t"] - last_print >= 1.0:
                        last_print = f["t"]
                        print(f"t={f['t']:6.1f}  {f['phase']:14s} {f['agl_ft']:6.0f} ft  {f['airspeed_kt']:4.0f} kt  "
                              f"vs {f['vertical_speed_fps']:6.1f}  elev {command['elevator']:+.3f}  "
                              f"thr {command['throttle']:.2f}  flaps {command['flaps']:.2f}  brake {command['brake']:.2f}")

                    if f["crashed"]:
                        print("FlightGear reports a crash - stopping.")
                        done = True
                    # done once it has come to a stop on the runway
                    elif f["phase"] == "landing" and f["gs_kt"] < 3.0:
                        stopped_since = stopped_since if stopped_since is not None else f["t"]
                        if f["t"] - stopped_since > 3.0:
                            print("aircraft stopped - done.")
                            done = True
                    else:
                        stopped_since = None
                if done:
                    break

    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("stopped.")

    finally:
        link.close()
        if log:
            FLIGHTS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path = FLIGHTS_DIR / f"{name}_{datetime.now():%Y%m%d_%H%M%S}.csv"
            log = pd.DataFrame(log)
            log.to_csv(path, index=False)
            if config is not None:
                json.dump(config, open(path.with_suffix(".json"), "w"), indent=2)
            print(f"log saved: {path}")
            summary(log)

    """Drop-in for fly.Autopilot: on_packet(o) -> [(features, command)] at 10 Hz."""

    def __init__(self, gains=GAINS):
        self.next_tick = None
        self.pid = {name: PIDController(g, GRID_S) for name, g in gains.items()}
        self.phase = "final_approach"
        self.wow_since = None
        self.started = False
        self.elevator = 0.0         # held where the flare left it after touchdown

    def on_packet(self, o):
        """Feed one 60 Hz packet; every 0.1 s of sim time, the latest one is used to command."""
        if self.next_tick is not None and o["t"] < self.next_tick - 1e-6:
            return []
        self.next_tick = (self.next_tick or o["t"]) + GRID_S
        if o["t"] >= self.next_tick:            # a gap in the data: restart the grid here
            self.next_tick = o["t"] + GRID_S
        f = features(o)
        return [(f, self.step(f))]

    def take_control(self, f):
        """First tick: seed every loop with where the aircraft is, so nothing jumps."""
        self.pid["vs_to_pitch"].reset(f["pitch_deg"])
        self.pid["speed_to_throttle"].reset(THROTTLE_START)
        self.started = True

    def update_phase(self, f):
        """final approach -> flare -> landing, never back (as fly.Autopilot)."""
        if f["wow"] == 1:
            self.wow_since = self.wow_since if self.wow_since is not None else f["t"]
        else:
            self.wow_since = None
        if self.phase != "landing" and self.wow_since is not None \
                and f["t"] - self.wow_since >= TOUCHDOWN_HOLD_S - 1e-6:
            self.phase = "landing"
        elif self.phase == "final_approach" and f["flare_flag"] == 1:
            self.phase = "flare"
            # the flare loops take over from the approach loops where those left off
            self.pid["drift_to_bank"].reset(self.pid["heading_to_bank"].u_n_1)
            self.pid["heading_to_rudder"].reset(self.pid["slip_to_rudder"].u_n_1)
        f["phase"] = self.phase

    def step(self, f):
        if not self.started:
            self.take_control(f)
        self.update_phase(f)
        p = self.pid

        if self.phase == "landing":
            # on the ground: the same rules as fly.py, so the roll-out does not differ
            return self.command(0.0, self.elevator, 0.0, 0.0, BRAKE_LEVEL if f["gs_kt"] < BRAKE_BELOW_KT else 0.0)

        # ---- lateral
        if self.phase == "final_approach":
            heading_ref = p["xtk_to_heading"](f["cross_track_error_m"], 0.0)
            bank_ref = p["heading_to_bank"](f["heading_error_deg"], heading_ref)
            rudder = p["slip_to_rudder"](f["sideslip_rad"], 0.0)
        else:
            bank_ref = p["drift_to_bank"](f["lateral_body_speed_fps"], 0.0)
            rudder = p["heading_to_rudder"](f["heading_error_deg"], 0.0)
        aileron = p["bank_to_aileron"](f["roll_deg"], bank_ref)

        # ---- longitudinal
        if self.phase == "final_approach":
            distance_m = AIM_POINT_M - f["along_track_m"]
            height_ref_ft = max(distance_m, 0.0) * math.tan(math.radians(GLIDESLOPE_REF_DEG)) / 0.3048
            vs_nominal = -f["gs_kt"] * 1.68781 * math.tan(math.radians(GLIDESLOPE_REF_DEG))
            vs_ref = vs_nominal + p["height_to_vs"](f["height_above_threshold_ft"], height_ref_ft)
            throttle = p["speed_to_throttle"](f["airspeed_kt"], V_REF_KT)
        else:
            vs_ref = -max(f["agl_ft"] / FLARE_TAU_S, FLARE_MIN_SINK_FPS)
            throttle = 0.0
        pitch_ref = p["vs_to_pitch"](f["vertical_speed_fps"], vs_ref)
        self.elevator = p["pitch_to_elevator"](f["pitch_deg"], pitch_ref)

        f.update(bank_ref_deg=bank_ref, pitch_ref_deg=pitch_ref, vs_ref_fps=vs_ref)     # for the log
        return self.command(aileron, self.elevator, rudder, throttle, 0.0)

    @staticmethod
    def command(aileron, elevator, rudder, throttle, brake):
        return dict(aileron=clip(aileron), elevator=clip(elevator), rudder=clip(rudder),
                    throttle=clip(throttle, 0.0, 1.0), flaps=FLAPS, brake=clip(brake, 0.0, 1.0))

docs.title: pid
docs.text:
FlightGear's , in Python.

The same algorithm as FlightGear's autopilot (src/Autopilot/pidcontroller.cxx, documented in $FG_ROOT/Docs/README.digitalfilters), with the same parameters, so gains written for one work in the other. It is ported instead of loaded inside FlightGear because FlightGear's autopilot runs inside the simulator and writes /controls/* directly: it would bypass the UDP link (fg_interface.py) and the 10 Hz pipeline (fly.py) the networks are evaluated with.

Velocity (incremental) form, "Roberts' digital PID":

ep_n  = beta  * r_n - y_n                  proportional error
e_n   =         r_n - y_n                  integral error
ed_n  = gamma * r_n - y_n                  derivative error, low-passed with Tf = alpha * Td
delta_u_n = Kp * [ (ep_n - ep_n-1) + Ts/Ti * e_n + Td/Ts * (edf_n - 2 edf_n-1 + edf_n-2) ]
u_n = clamp(u_n-1 + delta_u_n, u_min, u_max)

Clamping the OUTPUT of the velocity form is the anti-windup: there is no integral state to wind up. As in FlightGear, Ti must be > 0 (a large Ti means almost no integral action).

class PIDController:
    def __init__(self, gains: PIDGains, Ts: float):
        if gains.Ti <= 0.0:
            raise ValueError("Ti must be > 0, as in FlightGear (use a large Ti for almost no integral action)")
        self.g = gains
        self.Ts = Ts
        self.reset(0.0)

    def reset(self, u: float):
        """Start from output u, like FlightGear seeding u_n-1 from the output property when enabled:
        taking over from another controller (or the pilot) causes no jump."""
        self.u_n_1 = min(max(u, self.g.u_min), self.g.u_max)
        self.ep_n_1 = 0.0
        self.edf_n_1 = self.edf_n_2 = 0.0
        self.first = True

    def __call__(self, y_n: float, r_n: float) -> float:
        """One step: measurement y_n, reference r_n -> output u_n."""
        g, Ts = self.g, self.Ts

        ep_n = g.beta * r_n - y_n
        e_n = r_n - y_n
        if self.first:
            # FlightGear starts the velocity form with ep_n-1 = 0, so its first step jumps by Kp * ep_n.
            # Starting from the current error instead makes taking over bumpless.
            self.ep_n_1 = ep_n

        edf_n = 0.0
        if g.Td > 0.0:
            ed_n = g.gamma * r_n - y_n
            Tf = g.alpha * g.Td
            edf_n = self.edf_n_1 / (Ts / Tf + 1) + ed_n * (Ts / Tf) / (Ts / Tf + 1)
            if self.first:
                self.edf_n_1 = self.edf_n_2 = edf_n
        else:
            self.edf_n_1 = self.edf_n_2 = 0.0

        delta_u_n = g.Kp * ((ep_n - self.ep_n_1)
                            + (Ts / g.Ti) * e_n
                            + (g.Td / Ts) * (edf_n - 2 * self.edf_n_1 + self.edf_n_2))
        u_n = min(max(self.u_n_1 + delta_u_n, g.u_min), g.u_max)

        self.ep_n_1 = ep_n
        self.edf_n_2, self.edf_n_1 = self.edf_n_1, edf_n
        self.u_n_1 = u_n
        self.first = False
        return u_n

docs.title: 3. Colunas CONSTANTES (153) — presentes no CSV mas sem variação no seu voo
docs.text:
Essas ficam sempre no mesmo valor durante toda a gravação porque: - são recursos que o C172P de rodas fixas não usa (esqui, flutuador/pontoon, rotor de helicóptero, gear units 19–25 = trens extras de aeronaves maiores), - são chaves/luzes/disjuntores que você não mexeu durante o voo (magnetos, luzes de navegação, disjuntores — todos "True" o tempo todo), - ou são configurações que não mudam em voo normal (trim de aileron/leme, pressão ao nível do mar, seleção de tanque).

Alguns exemplos agrupados (lista completa nos comentários do script/gerada pelo parser): - Trim/controles secundários parados: aileron-trim, rudder-trim, speedbrake, spoilers, parking-lever - Trens de pouso "fantasma" (19 a 25): aeronaves com mais pernas de trem do que o C172P tem — sempre 0/False/1.0 - Flutuadores/hidro/esqui: todos zerados, já que a aeronave usada é a de rodas - Interruptores/luzes que você não usou nesse voo: nav-lights, strobe, landing-lights, taxi-light, dome-white, dome-red - Disjuntores (circuit-breakers): todos True (nenhum foi desarmado) - Chaves de motor: magnetos = 3 (ambos ligados), master-bat/alt = True, starter = False - Falhas simuladas: todas em estado "serviceable/OK" (você não ativou nenhuma falha) - Referências de navegação/altímetro: altimeter setting-inhg, nav radials selected-deg, heading-bug-deg — você não mexeu nesses ajustes durante a gravação

Essas colunas não atrapalham (o modelo pode simplesmente ignorá-las ou usá-las como features constantes), mas não carregam informação útil pro seu caso de uso.

docs.title: Observação sobre reamostragem
docs.text: Como discutido, sim_time não tem passo fixo (depende do FPS do FlightGear no momento — variou entre ~40Hz e ~60Hz nos seus dois pousos). Antes de treinar o modelo de imitation learning, recomenda-se reamostrar todas as colunas numéricas pra uma grade de tempo fixa (ex.: 20Hz ou 50Hz) usando interpolação linear em sim_time, em vez de tratar cada linha como um passo de tempo igual.

Como usar: python scripts/fgtape_to_csv.py arquivo.fgtape saida.csv

O CSV tem 247 colunas no total (frame + sim_time + 245 propriedades do FlightGear) — o mesmo esquema de colunas usado nos CSVs de pousos-helio (ver colunas_fgtape.md), já que os dois conjuntos saem do mesmo parser.

Essa análise usa os 15 voos da pasta voos-piloto (circuitos completos, voos normais e voos com vento/rajada/turbulência), em vez de só 2 pousos. Com mais voos e condições mais variadas, 112 das 245 propriedades variam em pelo menos um dos arquivos (contra 92 relatadas em colunas_fgtape.md, que olhou só 2 pousos). As outras 133 ficam constantes em todos os 15 voos.

Essas colunas não atrapalham (o modelo pode simplesmente ignorá-las ou usá-las como features constantes), mas não carregam informação útil pro caso de uso.

docs.title: Observação sobre reamostragem
docs.text: Como já discutido em colunas_fgtape.md, sim_time não tem passo fixo (depende do FPS do FlightGear no momento). Antes de treinar o modelo de imitation learning, recomenda-se reamostrar todas as colunas numéricas pra uma grade de tempo fixa (ex.: 20Hz ou 50Hz) usando interpolação linear em sim_time, em vez de tratar cada linha como um passo de tempo igual — e tratar cada um dos 15 voos como uma trajetória independente (não concatenar sem marcar o início/fim de cada arquivo).

docs.title: FlightGear
docs.text:
Tudo que o projeto precisa do simulador:

  • Aeronave e aeroporto — C172P, BIKF 02, posição inicial.
  • Protocolo UDP — campos trocados nas portas 5501 e 5502.
  • Launcher do FlightGear — scripts/launch_flightgear.sh, variáveis, caveat de macOS.

docs.title: Aeronave e aeroporto
docs.text: Cenário fixo em scripts/launch_flightgear.sh.

docs.title: Aeronave
docs.text: Cessna 172P (--aircraft=c172p) — monomotor a pistão, trem fixo. Modelo padrão do FlightGear.

docs.title: Aeroporto
docs.text: BIKF — Keflavík (Islândia), pista 02.

docs.title: Posição inicial
docs.text: Parâmetro Valor Fonte Latitude 63.937617°N 1ª linha das gravações Longitude -22.605467°W 1ª linha das gravações Heading 0.02° alinhado com a pista 02 Altitude 801 ft ~2995 m da cabeceira, antes do ponto de visada Velocidade indicada 82 kt aproximação inicial Elevator trim inicial -0.03 --prop:/controls/flight/elevator-trim=-0.03

docs.text:
Em src/fly.py:39-42:

Parâmetro Valor Latitude da cabeceira 02 63.96447778°N Longitude da cabeceira 02 -22.60545278°W Elevação da cabeceira 135 ft Heading da pista 0.02° Rampa de aproximação 3° Velocidade de referência (Vref) 65 kt

Essas constantes definem o sistema de coordenadas da pista usado pelas features (along_track_m, cross_track_m, height_above_threshold_ft, erro de rampa etc.).

docs.text: Flags fixos no launcher: --disable-real-weather-fetch, --disable-ai-traffic. Vento e turbulência vêm por argumento — ver Ajustar o clima.

docs.text: --timeofday=noon (meio-dia, sempre).

docs.title: Launcher do FlightGear
docs.text: scripts/launch_flightgear.sh inicia o simulador na pista 02 de BIKF e conecta o protocolo UDP.

docs.title: Uso
docs.text:
bash scripts/launch_flightgear.sh                  # calmo
bash scripts/launch_flightgear.sh 270 10           # vento cruzado 10 kt de 270°
bash scripts/launch_flightgear.sh 270 12 0.3       # idem + turbulência 0.3

Argumentos extras após o terceiro são passados ao FlightGear.

docs.text: Variável Padrão Para quê FG_APP detectado em /Applications, ~/Applications, DMG montado Caminho para FlightGear.app FG_ROOT ~/Library/Application Support/FlightGear/fgdata_2024_1 Pasta de dados do FlightGear

docs.title: O que o launcher faz
docs.text:
1. Resolve FG_APP (monta ~/Downloads/flightgear-2024.1.7-macos-universal.dmg se precisar).
  2. Copia config/flightgear/pfe_{out,in}.xml para $FG_ROOT/Protocol/.
  3. Executa:
FlightGear \
  --aircraft=c172p \
  --lat=63.937617 --lon=-22.605467 --altitude=801 --heading=0.02 --vc=82 \
  --timeofday=noon --disable-real-weather-fetch --disable-ai-traffic \
  --wind=<from>@<kt> --turbulence=<norm> \
  --prop:/controls/flight/elevator-trim=-0.03 \
  --prop:/sim/rendering/shaders/quality-level=1 \
  --generic=socket,out,60,127.0.0.1,5501,udp,pfe_out \
  --generic=socket,in,30,127.0.0.1,5502,udp,pfe_in \
  --telnet=5401

docs.title: Caveat de SO
docs.text:
Apenas macOS

O launcher usa hdiutil, caminhos .app do macOS e a estrutura $HOME/Library/Application Support. Em Linux/Windows você precisa:

  • encontrar o executável fgfs do FlightGear,
  • copiar os XMLs para o Protocol/ da sua instalação,
  • chamar o fgfs com os mesmos --generic=socket,....

Esse port está nas issues do projeto; abra uma e vincule a PR.

docs.title: Protocolo UDP
docs.text:
Comunicação entre FlightGear e autopiloto via UDP, CSV por linha. Definido em config/flightgear/pfe_out.xml e pfe_in.xml.

flowchart LR
  FG[FlightGear] -- "60 Hz · 5501 · pfe_out" --> AP[Autopiloto]
  AP -- "10 Hz · 5502 · pfe_in" --> FG

Host: 127.0.0.1.

docs.title: FlightGear → autopiloto (pfe_out.xml, porta 5501, 60 Hz)
docs.text:
28 campos, nessa ordem (idêntica a OUT_FIELDS em src/fg_interface.py):

sim_time, lat, lon, alt_ft, agl_ft, roll, pitch, heading, alpha,
side_slip_rad, roll_rate, pitch_rate, yaw_rate, ias, gs_kt, vs_fps,
vn_fps, ve_fps, v_lateral_fps, wind_kt, wind_from, turbulence,
elevator_trim, flaps, wow_nose, wow_left, wow_right, crashed

Separador: vírgula. Terminador: newline. Precisão típica %.4f.

O parser em FlightGearLink._parse descarta pacotes com contagem de campos incorreta, converte os wow_* em wow (qualquer roda no chão) e wow_main (apenas trem principal), e usa sim_time como timestamp.

docs.title: Autopiloto → FlightGear (pfe_in.xml, porta 5502, 30 Hz máx)
docs.text:
8 campos:

aileron, elevator, rudder, throttle, throttle0, flaps, brake_left, brake_right
  • throttle e throttle0 recebem o mesmo valor, para cobrir aeronaves que usam /controls/engines/current-engine/throttle ou /controls/engines/engine[0]/throttle.
  • brake_left e brake_right recebem o mesmo valor.
  • elevator é a posição do manche; fly.py subtrai o elevator_trim recebido antes de enviar (a rede prevê elevator_effective = yoke + trim).

docs.title: Instalação dos arquivos XML
docs.text:
O launcher copia pfe_out.xml e pfe_in.xml para $FG_ROOT/Protocol/ a cada execução, para que edições sejam captadas sem reinstalação. Flags finais do FlightGear:

--generic=socket,out,60,127.0.0.1,5501,udp,pfe_out
--generic=socket,in,30,127.0.0.1,5502,udp,pfe_in

docs.title: Taxa real de envio
docs.text: Embora o canal pfe_in esteja declarado em 30 Hz, fly.py escreve a 10 Hz (uma vez por janela de reamostragem). Ver Pipeline online.

docs.title: AKAER Autonomous Landing
docs.text:
Capstone project at Insper in partnership with Akaer. We train five feed-forward neural networks (one per control) to land a Cessna 172P in FlightGear via imitation learning, with a cascaded PID as the non-AI baseline.

This documentation targets two audiences:

  • people who need to reproduce the current experiment from scratch,
  • future students who will extend the project with new models (RNN, 1/2/4/8-network variants, comparisons).

Simulation only

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
This section describes how the team organizes work in the repository and how to extend the docs.

  • Repository workflow — issues, branches, PRs.
  • Docs workflow — how to edit and publish these pages.

docs.title: Repository workflow
docs.text:
Next steps live in the GitHub issues: PID, 1/2/4/8-network variants, RNN, alternative model, and results comparison.

  1. Pick an issue and assign yourself.
  2. Branch from main with a name tied to the issue (e.g. issue-7-rnn).
  3. Commit small, keep CI green.
  4. Open a pull request linked to the issue (Closes #N in the body).
  5. Request review from at least one teammate before merging.

Project README references to Pfe ak/ now map to src/ (code), scripts/ (launchers), and artifacts/ (outputs).

docs.title: Future-model issues
docs.text:
Each planned model has an empty page under explanation/models/future-*.md (e.g. future-rnn.md). When the issue is merged:

  1. Fill the matching page (PT and EN) using pid-baseline.md and five-networks.md as templates.
  2. Update the model matrix in explanation/models/index.md (status → Done, PR link).
  3. If the model changes the online pipeline, update explanation/online-pipeline.md.

docs.title: Docs workflow
docs.text: How to edit, preview, and publish the pages of this site.

docs.title: Install docs dependencies
docs.text:
Inside the project's virtualenv:

python -m pip install -r docs/requirements.txt

Versions are pinned in docs/requirements.txt so local build and CI match.

docs.title: Edit and preview
docs.text:
mkdocs serve

Opens http://127.0.0.1:8000. The server hot-reloads on edit. Switch PT ↔ EN from the language selector at the top.

docs.title: Verification build
docs.text:
Before opening a PR:

mkdocs build --strict

Must pass with zero warnings. CI runs the same command in .github/workflows/docs.yml.

docs.title: Bilingual rule
docs.text:
• PT is the default language: file page.md.
  • EN uses the suffix: file page.en.md.
  • Every page exists in both languages. Structure (sections, tables, diagrams) is identical — only prose changes.
  • nav in mkdocs.yml lists PT files only; the mkdocs-static-i18n plugin discovers the .en.md pair automatically.

docs.title: Writing conventions
docs.text:
• Every page starts with a one-line summary and a bullet list of outcomes.
  • Code blocks over screenshots for anything typeable; screenshots only for the FlightGear UI.
  • Admonitions: !!! note for context, !!! warning for the macOS-only launcher and damaged-flight CSVs, !!! tip for shortcuts.
  • Every how-to ends with an Expected output block the reader can diff against.
  • Diagrams as inline mermaid (not images); screenshots go under docs/assets/screenshots/.

docs.title: Deploy
docs.text:
Publishing is a two-step pipeline because the code repository is private and Vercel's free plan does not serve private organization repos.

  1. Build in GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/docs.yml): every push to main touching docs/**, mkdocs.yml, src/**, or the workflow itself installs the dependencies and runs mkdocs build --strict.
  2. Push to a public mirror: the Action publishes the generated site/ into the public repository hhenriqueN/akaer-landing-docs (branch main, orphan history — each deploy overwrites the previous one).
  3. Vercel serves the mirror: the Vercel project is connected to hhenriqueN/akaer-landing-docs with no build command — it just serves the static HTML from the repo root.

For the Action to be able to push to the mirror, the private repo stores the secret DOCS_DEPLOY_PAT (a fine-grained Personal Access Token with Contents: Read & write scoped to the mirror). If the token expires, create another one at https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens and replace the secret.

docs.title: New model
docs.text:
When a future-model issue is merged:

  1. Fill explanation/models/future-<name>.md and .en.md (today they're placeholders with just the title).
  2. Update the matrix in explanation/models/index.md.
  3. If the model changes the online pipeline, update explanation/online-pipeline.md.
  4. If it adds a new script, document it in reference/cli.md.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text:
Material to understand how and why the system works:

  • Architecture — data-flow overview.
  • Imitation learning — why behavioral cloning, data split, limits.
  • Online pipeline — filter, resample, z-score, phase machine.
  • Offline pipeline — from .fgtape to normalized folds.
  • Models — what exists today (ANN, PID) and what is planned.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Two paths: offline (training) and online (flight).

docs.title: Online path (in flight)
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  FG[FlightGear 60 Hz] -- "UDP 5501" --> IF[fg_interface.receive_all]
  IF --> LP["Butterworth 2nd order · 4 Hz"]
  LP --> ZOH[Zero-order hold · 10 Hz]
  ZOH --> FT["Features (lat__, lon__)"]
  FT --> N["z-score (clip ±5)"]
  N --> M{Controller}
  M --> |"5 networks"| NN["aileron · rudder · elevator · throttle · flaps"]
  M --> |"PID"| PID["cascaded loops"]
  NN --> POS[Post-process: clip, elevator-trim, brake rule]
  PID --> POS
  POS -- "UDP 5502 · 10 Hz" --> FG

Details in Online pipeline.

docs.title: Offline path (training)
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  TAPE["Data/raw/*.fgtape"] -->|scripts/fgtape_to_csv.py| CSV["Data/csv/voos-piloto/*.csv (60 Hz)"]
  CSV -->|external baseline-model| FOLDS["Data/processed/normalized_folds/fold_00_*.csv (10 Hz z-scored)"]
  FOLDS -->|src/ann.py| MODELS["artifacts/*.pt + normalization.json"]
  MODELS -->|src/replay.py| REPLAY["replay_*.png (open-loop)"]
  MODELS -->|src/fly.py| FG["FlightGear (closed-loop)"]

Details in Offline pipeline.

docs.title: Key decisions
docs.text: Decision Where Why 60 → 10 Hz with a 4 Hz filter fly.py + folds Aligns online and offline; removes > 30 Hz simulator noise Single normalization JSON artifacts/normalization.json Training and inference read the same file — hard to drift 5 independent networks src/ann.py Simple, interpretable, serves as a baseline for future variants 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 s lags HISTORY_LAGS in ann.py and live buffer in fly.py Gives temporality to a feed-forward model without an RNN Elevator = yoke + trim fly.py + elevator network Network learns the effective motion; fly.py subtracts trim before sending Rule-based brake fly.py landing phase No recorded flight has clean brake data to learn from

docs.title: Imitation learning
docs.text: The project uses behavioral cloning (BC): learn the state → command function from pilot demonstrations.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
Set Flights Use Train 11 flights from fold_00_train.csv Updates the weights Validation voo-normal2, voo-com-8-nos Picks the best epoch (no gradient) Test voo-2-com-16-nos Never enters ann.py; used by replay.py

Split is by whole flight, not by frames. This prevents temporal context leaking across splits.

docs.title: Target and loss
docs.text:
Each network predicts one continuous command:

Network Target column Physical command aileron laty__aileron_command aileron (-1..1) rudder laty__rudder_command rudder (-1..1) elevator lony__elevator_effective yoke + trim (-1..1) throttle lony__throttle_command throttle (0..1) flaps lon__flaps_state_norm flaps position (0..1)

Loss MSE over the z-scored target, optimizer Adam (lr=1e-3), MAX_EPOCHS=1000, BATCH_SIZE=1000, fixed seed (0).

Reference baseline printed by ann.py: RMSE of "always predict the pilot's mean". A useful network must stay well below that line.

docs.title: Why BC and not RL
docs.text:
• We have dozens of landing demonstrations, not a dense reward.
  • Training is deterministic and cheap (CPU is enough).
  • Clear baseline to compare future variants against (RNN, DAgger, RL).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Compounding error / covariate shift: closed-loop, small drifts take the aircraft to states the network never saw in training. Replay (open-loop) cannot detect this. Only FlightGear tests do.
  • Brake: no network learns to brake well — the pilot brakes late and sharply. fly.py falls back to a rule: brake=0.7 when GS < 45 kt in the landing phase.
  • landing phase: once all wheels have been on the ground for 0.5 s, the networks stop commanding aileron/rudder/throttle; fly.py forces zero. This prevents the network from accelerating or ground-looping.
  • Strong wind with damage: two training flights (voo-2-com-16-nos, voo-3-com-16-nos) have damage flags. Useful as a test; risky as a "clean" demonstration.

See Online pipeline for how the loop handles these limits in practice.

docs.title: Offline pipeline
docs.text:
How pilot recordings become training-ready data.

flowchart LR
  FG[Simulator records .fgtape] --> TAPE["Data/raw/*.fgtape"]
  TAPE -->|scripts/fgtape_to_csv.py| CSV["Data/csv/voos-piloto/*.csv (60 Hz · variable Δt)"]
  CSV -->|external baseline-model repo| FOLDS["Data/processed/normalized_folds/fold_00_{train,val}.csv (10 Hz · z-scored)"]
  FOLDS -->|src/ann.py| MODELS["artifacts/*.pt + normalization.json"]

docs.title: Stage 1 — .fgtape → raw CSV
docs.text:
scripts/fgtape_to_csv.py:

  • pure Python parser (stdlib),
  • reads the XML header with ~245 properties,
  • decompresses DEFLATE frames,
  • writes CSV with frame, sim_time and 245 columns.

Full schema: fgtape columns, Pilot flight columns.

Variable Δt

sim_time depends on simulator FPS during recording (typically 40–60 Hz). Do not treat rows as uniform time steps.

docs.title: Stage 2 — CSV → normalized folds
docs.text:
Processing lives in an external repository:

  • github.com/hhenriqueN/baseline-model

That pipeline:

  • resamples 60 Hz → 10 Hz (fixed grid),
  • derives runway-frame features (along-track, cross-track, glideslope errors, flare flag),
  • z-scores per feature with clip at ±5,
  • generates fold_{NN}_{train,val}.csv in Data/processed/normalized_folds/,
  • writes artifacts/normalization.json with the parameters used.

The same features and the same normalization JSON are used in src/fly.py — a critical point to avoid train/inference drift.

Current training uses fold_00 only

src/ann.py reads fold_00_train.csv + fold_00_val.csv, which together cover all 13 flights. Folds 01-04 exist in the external repo but are not used today.

docs.title: Stage 3 — folds → models
docs.text:
python src/ann.py (see Five networks).

Produces artifacts/<network>.pt with weights + metadata consumed by src/fly.py in production. Target normalization is computed during training and saved in the .pt; input normalization comes from the external normalization.json.

docs.title: Flights used
docs.text:
13 sessions in Data/csv/voos-piloto/ (full circuits, normal approaches, flights with wind 0 / 8 / 16 kt).

  • Train: 11 flights.
  • Validation: voo-normal2, voo-com-8-nos.
  • Test: voo-2-com-16-nos (never enters ann.py).

Damaged flights

voo-2-com-16-nos.csv and voo-3-com-16-nos.csv show wing/gear damage flags. Inspect before using as a "clean" demonstration. See Pilot flight columns.

docs.title: Online pipeline
docs.text: How src/fly.py processes data in real time.

docs.title: Rates
docs.text: Stage Rate FlightGear sends packets 60 Hz fly.py reads and filters 60 Hz (no packet dropped) fly.py resamples to the inference grid 10 Hz fly.py sends commands 10 Hz

docs.title: Detailed stages
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  P["UDP packet 60 Hz"] --> B["Butterworth 2nd order · 4 Hz"]
  B --> Z["ZOH · sample every 0.1 s"]
  Z --> F["Runway-frame features (along-track, cross-track, glideslope error, flare flag, ...)"]
  F --> N["z-score + clip ±5 (artifacts/normalization.json)"]
  N --> H["Buffer with lags 5/10/15 ticks"]
  H --> R["5 networks"]
  R --> C["Post-processing"]
  C --> U["UDP 5502"]

docs.title: 1. Low-pass filter
docs.text: 2nd-order Butterworth, cutoff 4 Hz, causal (fly.py:81-102). Removes high-frequency simulator noise (physics/rendering jitter).

docs.title: 2. Zero-order hold at 10 Hz
docs.text: Every 0.1 s, fly.py takes the latest filtered value. Fixed grid, identical to the training folds' frame_10hz.

docs.title: 3. Runway features
docs.text: fly.py converts lat/lon to runway-02 coordinates (along-track, cross-track in meters) and computes glideslope error, height above threshold, etc. Column names are identical to those used in training (lat__*, lon__*).

docs.title: 4. z-score with clip
docs.text: Reads artifacts/normalization.json: (x - mean) / std, clipped at ±5. Features with null entry in the JSON (sin/cos, flaps_state_norm, flare_flag) are not z-scored.

docs.title: 5. Temporal lags
docs.text: Live buffer with 5, 10, 15 ticks (0.5, 1.0, 1.5 s). Before enough history exists, the first value is repeated — same convention as add_history in ann.py.

docs.title: 6. Inference
docs.text:
The five networks run every 0.1 s. Inputs:

Network Inputs aileron, rudder 11 lat__* features × 4 (current + 3 lags) = 44 elevator, throttle 12 lon__* features × 4 = 48 flaps 4 features × 4 = 16

docs.title: 7. Post-processing
docs.text:
• All outputs: clip to [-1, 1] (or [0, 1] for throttle, flaps, brake).
  • elevator: the network emits elevator_effective (yoke + trim). fly.py subtracts the elevator_trim received from FlightGear before sending.
  • throttle: also sent as throttle0 (covers aircraft variants).

docs.title: Phase state machine
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> final_approach
  final_approach --> flare: AGL ≤ 20 ft
  flare --> landing: wheels on ground ≥ 0.5 s
  landing --> [*]
Phase Active networks Rules final_approach all — flare all — landing none for aileron/rudder/throttle brake = 0.7 if GS < 45 kt; aileron, rudder, throttle forced to 0

Transitions are monotonic (once in flare, no return to final_approach).

docs.title: Shutdown
docs.text: fly.py keeps logging until a stable touchdown is detected; then it writes artifacts/flights/<name>_<timestamp>.csv and exits. FlightGear must be closed manually.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Project model matrix. Each row links to the corresponding page.

Model Status Issue / PR Files Notes Five networks (one per control) Done merged src/ann.py, src/fly.py Current baseline PID (non-AI baseline) Done #10 src/pid.py, src/fly_pid.py Reference for comparison RNN Planned issues — — 1 unified network Planned issues — — 2 networks (lat/lon) Planned issues — — 4 networks Planned issues — — 8 networks Planned issues — —

To implement a variant, follow Add a new model.

docs.title: Five networks
docs.text: Current project baseline. One feed-forward network per control.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
All five networks share the same shape:

Linear(n_inputs, 64) → ReLU → Linear(64, 64) → ReLU → Linear(64, 1)
  • Loss: MSE over the z-scored target.
  • Optimizer: Adam, lr = 1e-3.
  • MAX_EPOCHS = 1000, BATCH_SIZE = 1000, fixed seed (0).
  • Best epoch picked by validation loss (passive early stopping).

docs.title: Inputs per network
docs.text:
Network Group Base features With lags (×4) aileron lat__* 11 44 rudder lat__* 11 44 elevator lon__* 12 48 throttle lon__* 12 48 flaps 4 fixed 4 16

Lags: 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 s = 5 / 10 / 15 ticks (HISTORY_LAGS). Each feature enters as "now" + "lag@5" + "lag@10" + "lag@15".

Base feature list: see Normalized folds.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
Network Target column Physical target aileron laty__aileron_command aileron (-1..1) rudder laty__rudder_command rudder (-1..1) elevator lony__elevator_effective yoke + trim; fly.py subtracts trim before sending throttle lony__throttle_command throttle (0..1) flaps lon__flaps_state_norm flaps position (0..1)

Target is z-scored during training with the training set's mean and std; these values are saved in artifacts/<network>.pt as y_mean, y_std and used by fly.py to undo the normalization.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
Each artifacts/<network>.pt stores:

Key Content model PyTorch state_dict input_cols Full input column list (with @5, @10, @15 suffixes) output_cols Target column name y_mean, y_std Target normalization (training) best_epoch Chosen epoch validation_flights Flights used to pick the best epoch

fly.py loads the checkpoint with torch.load(..., weights_only=False).

docs.title: Why five networks
docs.text:
• Transparency: each network is small, trains fast (CPU is enough), and is easy to inspect.
  • Diagnosis: separate learning curves reveal which command is hardest (flaps is usually easiest; elevator the most sensitive).
  • Baseline: future variants (1, 2, 4, 8 networks, RNN) are compared against this one.

docs.title: Reconsider when
docs.text:
• Sample rate (10 Hz) or lags (5/10/15) change — rebuild fly.py's pipeline and regenerate folds in the external repo.
  • normalization.json changes — retrain everything.
  • Features added/removed — update NETWORKS in ann.py and the feature list in fly.py, using the same names.

docs.title: PID (baseline)
docs.text: Cascaded controller, no neural networks, used as a reference.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Show the scenario is controllable with tuned classical control — and give an honest performance reference the AI models must at least match.

docs.title: Cascaded structure
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  CT[Cross-track error] --> HD[Heading error]
  HD --> BK[Target bank]
  BK --> AI[Aileron]

  SS[Sideslip] --> RD[Rudder]

  H[Height vs 3° glide path] --> VS[Target vertical speed]
  VS --> PI[Target pitch]
  PI --> EL[Elevator]

  V[Airspeed] --> TH[Throttle]
  • Lateral (approach): cross-track → heading error → bank → aileron. Sideslip → rudder.
  • Longitudinal: height vs 3° glide path (aim point 300 m past threshold) → vertical speed → pitch → elevator.
  • Speed: airspeed → throttle (Vref 65 kt).
  • Flaps: fixed at 1.0 (same as the recorded flights).

In flare (AGL ≤ 20 ft):

  • target vertical speed decays exponentially (vs_ref = -agl / 3.0, floor 1.5 fpm),
  • throttle to idle,
  • rudder aligns the heading,
  • aileron kills the lateral drift.

docs.title: Velocity-form PID
docs.text:
src/pid.py implements the same discrete PID used by FlightGear's autopilot ($FG_ROOT/Docs/README.digitalfilters):

ep_n       = beta * r_n - y_n           (proportional)
e_n        = r_n - y_n                  (integral)
ed_n       = gamma * r_n - y_n          (filtered derivative)
Δu_n       = Kp * [ (ep_n - ep_{n-1})
                   + Ts/Ti * e_n
                   + Td/Ts * (edf_n - 2*edf_{n-1} + edf_{n-2}) ]
u_n        = clamp(u_{n-1} + Δu_n, u_min, u_max)

Per-loop parameters: Kp, Ti, Td, u_min, u_max, beta (setpoint weight in the proportional term), alpha (derivative filter Tf = alpha * Td), gamma (setpoint weight in the derivative; 0 = derivative-on-measurement).

The velocity form removes the integral state — anti-windup lives in the output clamp.

docs.title: Practical differences vs networks
docs.text: Item Networks (fly.py) PID (fly_pid.py) Input UDP packets filtered at 4 Hz raw UDP packets Resampling ZOH to 10 Hz latest packet every 0.1 s Normalization z-score with normalization.json none Command rate 10 Hz 10 Hz Phases final_approach → flare → landing same Brake rule (brake=0.7 if GS < 45 kt) same rule

docs.title: Why not use FlightGear's built-in PID
docs.text: FlightGear's autopilot writes directly to /controls/*, bypassing UDP and ignoring the 10 Hz rate the networks use — the comparison would be unfair. fly_pid.py reimplements the PID in Python with the same loop and the same limits.

docs.title: Gains
docs.text:
The eleven PIDs are tuned for C172P dynamics on BIKF runway 02. They live in GAINS inside src/fly_pid.py and are saved next to each flight log in artifacts/flights/pid_<timestamp>.json.

Changing gains: edit GAINS, run CONTROLLER=pid bash scripts/run_flight.sh ..., compare via the log.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Two-step tutorial for first-time users:

  1. Installation — Python, dependencies and FlightGear.
  2. First landing — from git clone to a landing in the simulator.

After that, use the recipes in How-to.

docs.title: First landing
docs.text:
Goal: from zero to an autonomous landing in FlightGear. Prerequisite: Installation complete.

Expected result:

  • five .pt files in artifacts/,
  • a replay_<flight>.png with pilot vs networks comparison,
  • a successful landing in FlightGear with a log in artifacts/flights/.

docs.title: 1. Train the five networks
docs.text:
python src/ann.py

The current configuration trains aileron, rudder, elevator, throttle and flaps. Each network has two 64-unit hidden layers and 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 s history. All epochs run; weights from the best validation epoch are kept.

Expected output (abridged):

13 flights: 11 train, 2 validation (voo-normal2, voo-com-8-nos)

aileron   best epoch  ...   validation RMSE 0.0xxx   (guess the average: 0.yyyy)
rudder    best epoch  ...
elevator  best epoch  ...
throttle  best epoch  ...

python src/replay.py voo-2-com-16-nos

docs.title: Add a new model
docs.text: Recipe for implementing one of the planned variants (RNN, 1/2/4/8 networks) or proposing a new model.

docs.title: Recommended flow
docs.text:
1. Open or claim an issue on the project. Work on a dedicated branch tied to it.
  2. Reuse the existing pipeline:
  3. Inputs and normalization: src/ann.py + artifacts/normalization.json.
  4. Online loop: src/fly.py already handles UDP, filtering, resampling, z-score and the state machine. Prefer creating src/fly_<model>.py that imports fg_interface.py and reuses the pipeline helpers.
  5. Launcher: scripts/launch_flightgear.sh does not need to change — the model reads 5501 and writes 5502.
  6. Choose the controller interface:
  7. 5 networks (current) — one per control;
  8. N networks — group commands by nature (lat/lon, or everything in one);
  9. RNN — carry state across 10 Hz steps; the add_history helper in ann.py becomes unnecessary if the model has its own memory.
  10. Train with fold_00_{train,val}.csv. Keep validation flights (voo-normal2, voo-com-8-nos) and the test flight (voo-2-com-16-nos) unchanged. Save artifacts under a dedicated prefix (e.g. artifacts/rnn/).
  11. Validate open-loop with a replay compatible with the new architecture.
  12. Run closed-loop in FlightGear on the same scenarios (calm + 270@10 + 270@12 turb 0.3).
  13. Update the docs:
  14. fill in the empty page under docs/explanation/models/future-<model>.md;
  15. add a row in the Models matrix;
  16. document the CLI in CLI reference.
  17. Open a PR linked to the issue.

  • the same command rate (10 Hz),

  • the same weather scenarios.

docs.title: Fly in FlightGear (ANN or PID)
docs.text:
Run the controller closed-loop against FlightGear.

macOS

scripts/launch_flightgear.sh has only been tested on macOS. See FlightGear launcher.

docs.title: Single command
docs.text:
Calm wind (150° / 3.7 kt, like voo-normal*):

bash scripts/run_flight.sh

10 kt wind from 270°:

bash scripts/run_flight.sh 270 10

Wind + turbulence:

bash scripts/run_flight.sh 270 12 0.3

CONTROLLER=pid bash scripts/run_flight.sh 270 10

docs.title: Separate terminals
docs.text:
# terminal 1
python src/fly.py             # or: python src/fly_pid.py

# terminal 2 (wait ~3 s)
bash scripts/launch_flightgear.sh 270 10

docs.title: What happens
docs.text:
1. fly.py opens UDP port 5501 and waits for FlightGear packets at 60 Hz.
  2. The launcher starts FlightGear at BIKF runway 02, Cessna 172P, 2995 m from threshold, 801 ft, 82 kt. UDP protocols are auto-copied into $FG_ROOT/Protocol/.
  3. fly.py filters the data (Butterworth 4 Hz), resamples to 10 Hz, applies z-score, runs the five networks, and sends commands on UDP port 5502.
  4. Phases: final_approach → flare (AGL ≤ 20 ft) → landing (wheels on ground 0.5 s).
  5. fly.py exits by itself after touchdown and saves its log; close FlightGear manually.
