docs.text:
• artifacts/flights/<name>_<timestamp>.csv — features + commands at 10 Hz.
  • artifacts/flightgear.log — simulator stdout/stderr.

More in Online pipeline.

docs.title: Replay a recorded flight
docs.text: Compares network-predicted commands against the actual pilot flight, open-loop (the networks do not change the trajectory).

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
python src/replay.py voo-2-com-16-nos

Without an argument the script uses voo-normal3. Recordings are read from Data/csv/voos-piloto/.

docs.title: What replay does
docs.text:
1. Rebuilds network inputs with the same pipeline as fly.py (filter, features, z-score).
  2. Compares those inputs against the normalized folds (when available) — reports max |Δ| and % within ±0.05.
  3. Compares predicted commands against recorded pilot commands — reports RMSE per control and pilot min/max range.
  4. Saves artifacts/replay_<flight>.png with 6 subplots (aileron, rudder, elevator, throttle, flaps, brake), with flare and touchdown markers.

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
inputs: max |Δ|=... (99.X% within ±0.05)
RMSE aileron ...   RMSE rudder ...   RMSE elevator ...   ...
plot: artifacts/replay_voo-2-com-16-nos.png

Open-loop ≠ landing

Replay measures imitation on the recorded pilot trajectory. It does not prove that the network can land on its own — only closed-loop FlightGear runs do.

docs.title: Which flight to pick
docs.text:
• voo-2-com-16-nos is the official test set (never used in training).
  • Any other CSV in Data/csv/voos-piloto/ also works.

Damaged flights

voo-2-com-16-nos.csv and voo-3-com-16-nos.csv show wing/gear damage flags (hard landing in heavy wind). Useful as a test, but inspect before using as a "clean" demo. See Pilot flight columns.

docs.text: Trains aileron, rudder, elevator, throttle, flaps from the data in Data/processed/normalized_folds/.

Reads fold_00_train.csv and fold_00_val.csv. Runs MAX_EPOCHS epochs and keeps the weights from the epoch with the lowest validation loss.

docs.text:
macOS only

The launcher relies on hdiutil, macOS .app paths, and $HOME/Library/Application Support. On Linux/Windows you need to:

  • find your FlightGear fgfs executable,
  • copy the XMLs into your installation's Protocol/,
  • invoke fgfs with the same --generic=socket,... flags.

This port is tracked in the project issues; please open one and link your PR.

docs.title: UDP protocol
docs.text:
Communication between FlightGear and the autopilot via UDP, one CSV line per packet. Defined in config/flightgear/pfe_out.xml and pfe_in.xml.

flowchart LR
  FG[FlightGear] -- "60 Hz · 5501 · pfe_out" --> AP[Autopilot]
  AP -- "10 Hz · 5502 · pfe_in" --> FG

Host: 127.0.0.1.

docs.title: FlightGear → autopilot (pfe_out.xml, port 5501, 60 Hz)
docs.text:
28 fields in this order (identical to OUT_FIELDS in src/fg_interface.py):

sim_time, lat, lon, alt_ft, agl_ft, roll, pitch, heading, alpha,
side_slip_rad, roll_rate, pitch_rate, yaw_rate, ias, gs_kt, vs_fps,
vn_fps, ve_fps, v_lateral_fps, wind_kt, wind_from, turbulence,
elevator_trim, flaps, wow_nose, wow_left, wow_right, crashed

Separator: comma. Terminator: newline. Typical precision %.4f.

The parser in FlightGearLink._parse discards packets with wrong field counts, derives wow (any wheel on ground) and wow_main (main gear only), and uses sim_time as the timestamp.

docs.title: Autopilot → FlightGear (pfe_in.xml, port 5502, 30 Hz max)
docs.text:
8 fields:

aileron, elevator, rudder, throttle, throttle0, flaps, brake_left, brake_right
  • throttle and throttle0 receive the same value, covering aircraft that use either /controls/engines/current-engine/throttle or /controls/engines/engine[0]/throttle.
  • brake_left and brake_right get the same value.
  • elevator is the yoke position; fly.py subtracts the received elevator_trim before sending (the network predicts elevator_effective = yoke + trim).

docs.title: XML installation
docs.text:
The launcher copies pfe_out.xml and pfe_in.xml to $FG_ROOT/Protocol/ on every run, so edits are picked up without manual install. Final FlightGear flags:

--generic=socket,out,60,127.0.0.1,5501,udp,pfe_out
--generic=socket,in,30,127.0.0.1,5502,udp,pfe_in

docs.title: Actual send rate
docs.text: Even though the pfe_in channel is declared at 30 Hz, fly.py writes at 10 Hz (once per resampling tick). See Online pipeline.
